extractor.note: Whole file grep-counted for the theme's search terms plus 'Wesensschau', 'free variation', 'immutable' and 'essential intuition' ('free variation', 'essential intuition' and 'immutable' return nothing; 'Wesensschau' occurs once, at § 1). Closely read § 1 (lines 25-56), § 8 (426-529), § 13 (820-891), § 16 (1032-1073), and the opening paragraphs of §§ 37, 45 and 50.

coverage_note: Covers § 1 (the Husserlian doctrine of eidetic intuition and regional ontology as Henry reports it), § 8 (phenomenology as science of the essence of the phenomenon), § 13 (the ambiguity of Dasein; essence and ontic determination), § 16 (the autonomy of the essence), and the opening paragraphs of § 37, § 45 and § 50. Sections II (§§ 17-36) and the bulk of Section III (§§ 38-49, 51-70), where the term saturates, were keyword-scanned only and not read paragraph by paragraph.

units.claim: Empiricism's own thesis is said to presuppose an intuition of the essence of sensible experience, and that presupposition is presented as establishing that an eidetic intuition exists.
units.quote: The intuition presupposed by empiricism, of the essence of sensible experience, puts us in presence, at least once, of the existence of an eidetic intuition.

units.claim: The commentary glosses the self-refutation of empiricism as a proof of the reality of Wesensschau, the sole occurrence of that term in the commentary.
units.quote: the self-refutation of empiricism is thus a proof of the reality of *Wesensschau*

units.claim: Being is said to distribute itself into regions, each with its own eidetic structure, to which correspond rigorously determined types of donative intuition.
units.quote: distributes itself, in conformity with the very manner in which it presents itself, into a plurality of regions to which correspond rigorously determined types of donative intuition

units.claim: Phenomenology is defined as the science of the essence of the phenomenon, and it is because being is understood as that essence that Heidegger can call phenomenology ontology.
units.quote: *Phenomenology is the science of the essence of the phenomenon.* It is because he understands being as the essence of phenomenon that Heidegger can say that phenomenology is the science of being and, as such, ontology.

units.claim: The inevitability of the fall from the purity of the essence into ontic determination is proposed as inscribed in the essence itself, as an eidetic character rather than a lapse of exposition.
units.quote: as an eidetic character, as a property of the essence itself, that historializes itself in the essence in conformity with its own will

units.claim: On the monist structure the essence of manifestation is not manifestation of self: what manifests itself is the existent, not the essence.
units.quote: The essence of manifestation is not the *manifestation of self*. It is not the essence that manifests itself; it is the existent.

units.claim: The essence is called autonomous because effective phenomenality arises within it, and that autonomy is named the Selbstandigkeit of ontological knowledge.
units.quote: Effective phenomenality arises in the very bosom of the essence, because the essence objectifies itself under the form of a horizon that *shows itself*.

units.claim: The dissimulation of the essence is referred not to a failing of thought but to the essence itself and to the ontological structure of reality.
units.quote: Thus the dissimulation of the essence was referred, not to an incomprehensible failing of thought, but *to this essence itself*, to the ontological structure of reality.

units.claim: Because it does not manifest itself in the milieu of visibility, the essence is called invisible, and that invisibility is presented as its reality rather than a privation.
units.quote: insofar as it is *neither this nor that*, *the essence is invisible*
